To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have implemented a GPU accelerated signed log domain FFT non binary LDPC decoder with parallel and sequential node updating, and that the performance of the sequential CUDA decoder is very close to the parallel one.

we have implemented a CUDA based signed log domain FFT message passing decoder for non binary LDPC code which is about 20 times faster than the equivalent software implementation on a single CPU core.

we present a CUDA based implementation of a signed FFT decoder for nonbinary LDPC codes which is about 10 times faster than the fastest known implementation on a CPU, that we show that the layered update scheme for non binary LDPC decoders is well suited to be implemented on a GPU, and that we achieve a further speedup by employing quasi cyclic non binary irregular LD PC codes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the efficient implementation of message passing decodings of non binary LDPC code using GPUs.
the efficient implementation of message passing decodings of non binary LDPC code on GPUs, and the investigation of the impact of different scheduling schemes on their decoding performance.
the efficient implementation of non binary LDPC decoders on state of the art GPU hardware.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the layered CUDA implementation of the FFT decoder outperforms the flooding CUDA implementation of the same decoder.

the CUDA implementation of the sequential decoder for quasi cyclic non binary irregular LDLC codes is able to achieve an overall speedup of up to 30 times in comparison to a single core CPU implementation on an Intel Core i7 processor.
the GPU accelerated layered decoder is able to achieve a speedup of up to 10x compared to the sequential CPU implementation and a speedup of 2x compared to the GPU accelerated flooding decoder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a CUDA based implementation of a signed domain FFT decoder for quasi cyclic non binary irregular LDLC codes.
we present the first CUDA implementation of a non binary LDPC decoder with layered update scheme.
the proposed GPU implementations allow to decode non binary LDPC code with a high speedup and a very low latency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the layered update rule can be efficiently implemented on a GPU, yielding a speedup of about 2.5x for quasi cyclic non binary irregular LDLC codes of rate 0.5 and block length 20480.
the layered update rule can be efficiently parallelized and thus is a viable alternative to the traditional flooding rule.
the performance of non binary LDPC decoders on GPUs can be significantly improved by exploiting the parallelism of message passing decoding algorithms.
